messages:
Noah Kim: Hey team — quick onboarding question. I added benefits when I joined 2024-08-01 but I forgot to add my domestic partner for medical and also want to start an FSA. The portal only had spouse/child options. What paperwork do I need and how will this affect payroll deductions (esp FSA pre-tax amounts)?

Tessa (People Ops): Welcome, Noah! Domestic partners are allowed. We need a signed domestic partner affidavit + a proof of shared residence dated within last 90 days (lease, utility, bank). I'll DM the affidavit PDF. For FSA, you can elect within 30 days of hire — note FSA elections are per-calendar-year and have different proration rules.

Noah Kim: Thanks. My first paycheck already went out last Friday before I realized. If I enroll partner retro to 8/1 and elect FSA now, will payroll do catch-up pre-tax deductions? Concerned about a big hit to my next paycheck.

Luis (Benefits): Short answer: yes for premiums we can request retro, but FSA contributions are usually forward-looking and can't be made retro to before your enrollment date unless carrier/plan admin allows; exceptions are rare. For medical premiums, if carrier approves retro to 2024-08-01 we'll work with payroll to prorate. For FSA, you can set the full annual contribution now and payroll will spread deductions over remaining pay periods — we can also split catch-up if needed.

Noah Kim: So FSA can't cover expenses incurred before enrollment date, right? e.g., dentist appointment on 7/28 won't be eligible?

Luis (Benefits): Correct — FSA eligible expenses must occur on or after your FSA effective date. If we can retro the FSA effective date (rare), then maybe, but typically no. If you need help with eligible expense timing, send details to benefits@redwood.com and we'll advise.

Tessa (People Ops): Tagging @PayrollBot to confirm proration behavior and options to split large deductions across pays. Also FYI payroll cutoff is 3pm PT two business days before payday.

PayrollBot: PayrollBot: For retro medical premiums, payroll computes a prorated catch-up deduction to recover missed premium amounts and can split that catch-up across next 1-3 pay periods on employee request. For FSA elections made after year start, payroll will calculate remaining per-paycheck deductions based on the elected annual amount and remaining pay periods. We do not retroactively apply FSA contributions to past paychecks unless plan admin approves a retro effective date.

Noah Kim: Got it. Also my partner is enrolled through COBRA until 2024-08-20. Should I enroll now or wait?

Luis (Benefits): Enroll now and include "COBRA" + your partner's COBRA end date in the email to benefits@redwood.com. We'll coordinate termination with the COBRA administrator once new coverage is effective. Enrolling early helps avoid gaps.

Noah Kim: Uploaded affidavit + utility bill to benefits@redwood.com, subject line: "DOMESTIC PARTNER + FSA + COBRA (RETRO)". Also set FSA election in Workday. Thanks!

Luis (Benefits): Received. We'll review docs and request retro effective dates where possible. If payroll needs to apply a catch-up, we'll DM you before processing to agree on splitting. Expect confirmation in 2 business days.

Tessa (People Ops): Thanks Noah — noted on payroll side too. Ping here if you don't see confirmation in 48 hours. :thumbsup:

Noah Kim: Perfect, appreciate the help everyone :)
